intent: Test linux_configuration/scripts/single_use/fixes/lib/bt_audio.sh, fourth of the 16 untested fixes/lib libs, and fix a production bug the tests exposed: check_pipewire_health could never see a healthy PipeWire. The lib reaches 96.97% and STAYS on the allowlist -- the four remaining lines are unreachable by construction, for the instrument reason recorded below.
scope: linux_configuration/scripts/single_use/fixes/lib/bt_audio.sh (one-line behaviour fix at the timeout call)
Non-goal: the remaining twelve untested fixes/lib libs
meta/shell-coverage-allowlist.txt is deliberately UNCHANGED: bt_audio.sh does not meet the 100% bar
changes: Fixed lib/bt_audio.sh:21. It read `if timeout 3 _run_as_user wpctl status`, but `timeout` is a binary and cannot invoke a shell function, so the call always failed with rc=127 ('timeout: failed to run command _run_as_user'). check_pipewire_health therefore reported PipeWire hung on EVERY run and restarted a healthy audio stack every time. Now `_run_as_user timeout 3 wpctl status`, which keeps the 3-second bound but puts it inside the sudo'd command where it can actually run. Confirmed _run_as_user is never exported, so no caller relied on the old shape.

Added test_bt_audio.sh covering check_pipewire_health (wpctl absent, responsive, and hung), _run_as_user (SUDO_USER set and the USER fallback), _restart_pipewire_stack, and set_audio_profile (empty TARGET_MAC, pactl absent, no matching card, the SBC-XQ switch, and a healthy profile left alone).

Added test_bt_audio_connect.sh covering connect_device: empty TARGET_MAC, already connected, paired with a successful direct connect, a failed direct connect that falls through to scan-and-fail, a full scan/pair/trust/connect for an unpaired device, and a device found by the scan whose connection never becomes healthy.

Added test_bt_audio_health.sh covering _check_connection_health: not connected, services resolved on the first probe, services resolving only after the full adapter reset (driven by a counting dbus-send stub), and services that never resolve at all.

Added _t_stub_stdin to lib_test_core.sh. Stub bodies are data containing $1 and ${VAR} that must survive verbatim, and writing them as single-quoted strings tripped SC2016 on every use; reading the body from stdin via a quoted heredoc keeps it literal with no suppression.

Made the bluetoothctl stubs drain their stdin (`cat >/dev/null`) before exiting. The real tool consumes its whole input; a stub that read one line and exited closed the pipe early, so the writing `{ ...; } |` block took SIGPIPE partway through and its later lines never ran. That alone was worth 90.91% -> 96.97%.

verification.evidence: bt_audio (pipewire): 20 passed; bt_audio (connect): 15 passed; bt_audio (health): 12 passed; all 0 failed. All fixes lib test files passed, so bt_report, bt_pairing, bt_adapter and the eight pacman_hook_stall suites stay green.
bt_audio.sh: 128/132 lines = 96.97%, identical to the first run. Two matching runs, so the figure is not timing-dependent.

verification.command: Read the uncovered lines before deciding whether the lib could be cleared
verification.evidence: Lines 90, 113, 137 and 157 are each the `} |` that closes a piped block -- the pipe OPERATOR joining the block to `bluetoothctl`, not a statement. Proven executable with a marker file: a `{ echo a; echo b; } | consumer` block writes every marker even though bash's xtrace never reports the left-hand side, because a pipe's LHS runs in a subshell whose xtrace is not captured. So the lines run; kcov cannot attribute them.

Reproduced the bug directly before fixing: "timeout: failed to run command '_run_as_user': No such file or directory", rc=127. After the fix the healthy branch is reachable and its test ('PipeWire is responsive') passes.

verification.command: shfmt -w on HEAD's bt_audio.sh, then diff against HEAD
verification.evidence: shfmt REWRITES HEAD's `{ ...; } \` + `| bluetoothctl` one-liners into multi-line blocks ending in `} |`. The pre-commit hook runs `shfmt -w` on every staged shell file, so this reformat is unavoidable on any commit touching the file and reverting it is not stable. That is why 96.97% is accepted rather than restored to the pre-format 100%.

verification.command: grep -lnE '^[[:space:]]*\|' and grep -lE '\}[[:space:]]*\|[[:space:]]*$' over all 22 fixes/lib libs
verification.evidence: The continuation-pipe form is confined to the bluetooth family: bt_adapter.sh carries the pre-format flavour and bt_audio.sh the post-shfmt one. None of the remaining twelve untested libs has either, so this artifact does not block the rest of the campaign.

risks: bt_audio.sh stays on the allowlist at 96.97%. The four uncovered lines are `} |` pipe operators that kcov instruments but bash never attributes a statement to -- the same defect (a) class as bt_adapter.sh line 97, in a third flavour. Clearing either lib needs meta/scripts/lib/shell_coverage_lines.py to exclude these forms, which changes the denominator for every measured lib and must land on its own.

An earlier measurement of this lib read 99/99 = 100.00%. That number measured the file BEFORE pre-commit's shfmt reformatted it, and is superseded by 128/132 = 96.97% here. The reformat raised the denominator from 99 to 132 by splitting six one-line blocks into their constituent statements.

The bt_audio.sh fix changes runtime behaviour: fix_bluetooth.sh will now SKIP the PipeWire/WirePlumber restart when wpctl answers within 3 seconds, where before it restarted the audio stack on every run. That is the intended behaviour of the function as written.
bt_audio.sh is now exactly 250 lines, i.e. AT the repo cap. The next edit to it must split the file; a comment trim will not buy room twice.
rollback: git revert the commit; it adds three test files, one core helper and a one-line behaviour fix, and touches no allowlist entry.
After rollback, run bash linux_configuration/scripts/single_use/fixes/lib/tests/run_all.sh and confirm the remaining suites pass. No coverage gate changes, since bt_audio.sh stays exempt either way.
